name: Client Recovery Through Fast Alignment
author: Maya Okafor
description: Realigned the internal team in under 48 hours before responding externally, recovering a major at-risk account.

strategy: Protect a top-10 ARR account that had escalated three issues in two weeks.
Demonstrate that customer-success can run an internal rapid-response loop without involving the exec team.
Aligned with our 'trust before throughput' company value.
Mattered because losing this account would trigger a board-level escalation.
workPlan: Triage call within 4 hours of the escalation email; one written response promised within 48.
Milestones: internal alignment doc by EOD day 1, joint customer call by day 2, written commitment by day 3.
Tasks: pull all support history, draft the response, get sign-off from CS lead and account exec.
Resources: 1 day of CS lead time, async review from product, no extra budget.
people: Maya (CS lead) drove it. Daniel (account exec) brought the relationship history. Priya (product) sanity-checked the technical fix.
Maya = Accountable, Daniel = Consulted, Priya = Consulted, exec team = Told.
What worked: Daniel's calm framing of the customer's actual fear (vs. the surface complaint).
Held back from looping in the exec team until we had a real plan to share.
operations: Used the existing escalation runbook but compressed every step from days to hours.
Biggest barrier: the support history was spread across three tools. Maya manually consolidated it.
Functions involved: Customer Success, Sales, Product.
To repeat: a single canonical view of customer history and a pre-agreed 48-hour SLA for top-tier accounts.
results: Account renewed for 18 months at +12% expansion, two weeks ahead of the original renewal date.
Quantitative: $480k ARR retained, ~6 hours of CS lead time invested, zero exec escalation.
Qualitative: customer CSM described us as 'the most aligned vendor they work with'; internal team morale lifted.
Repeatable lesson: align internally before responding externally — even when the customer is loudest about wanting a fast reply.

playbook.repeatableRule: When a top account escalates, align internally before you respond externally — and let the calmest voice frame the customer's real fear.
playbook.suggestedNextWin: Pilot a 'unified customer history' view for the top 20 accounts so the next 4-hour triage doesn't need manual consolidation.

sdj.save: The 4h-triage / 48h-response cadence and the discipline of holding execs in the loop only after a plan exists.
sdj.delete: Manual consolidation of customer history across three tools — it cost the most and added the least.
sdj.join: Combine with any future 'top-account playbook' work so the runbook and the data layer ship together.
